journal: Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) journals (shared author guidelines)
snapshot_note: Rules that the RSC Advances and RSC Medicinal Chemistry author guidelines state word for word. Article types, page limits, fees and journal-specific reporting rules differ: SubmitReady reads the journal's own page on every run.

csl_style.title: Royal Society of Chemistry
csl_style.note: Vancouver-type numbered style with superscript citation numbers, usually after the punctuation.

requirements.quote: Use of the template is optional for our journals.

requirements.rule: Single-paragraph abstract of about 50 to 250 words
Conflicts of interest statement in the manuscript; 'There are no conflicts to declare' if none
requirements.quote: This statement is required for all submitted manuscripts.

requirements.rule: Data availability statement with every article
requirements.quote: A data availability statement (DAS) is required to be submitted alongside all articles.

requirements.rule: Funding sources and any AI tool use declared in the Acknowledgements
requirements.quote: You should also declare all sources of funding and any use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at this point.

requirements.rule: Author contributions section, preferably in CRediT terms
requirements.quote: In the interests of transparency, we strongly encourage authors of research articles to include an "Author contributions" section in their manuscript, for publication in the final article.
It’s important you use Vancouver style (not Harvard style).

requirements.rule: Superscript citation numbers, usually after the punctuation, in order of appearance
requirements.quote: Use superscript numbers to show the reference source of statements in the text – for example, reactive small molecule species.3

requirements.rule: Figures, schemes and charts as TIFF at 600 dpi or more (EPS or PDF accepted), 8.3 or 17.1 cm wide
requirements.quote: Figures, Schemes and Charts should be supplied as TIFF files, with a resolution of 600 dpi or greater.

requirements.rule: Conclusions that interpret the key results, not a summary of the abstract
requirements.quote: The conclusions should not summarise information already present in the article or abstract.
Suitable characterisations of compounds must be included

requirements.rule: Check the journal's own page for article types, length, the table of contents graphic and fees
